preamble: Characters in a certain opera are asterisked.

clue.text: *O for a pageant including an alien from Leicester!

indicators.note: including means the altered word wraps around the other piece and holds it inside
'O for A' asks the solver to put the O where an A stood, a straight swap of one letter
taking something from a word removes those letters from it, leaving the rest

parts.note: taken as written; its first A is swapped out
the letter O, taken as written
ET is the film alien
the English city, taken as written

explanation.surface: An excited cry for a carnival procession featuring a visitor from another world, in the English Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: The alien's two letters are not together in the city's name: lift out the first E and the T separately. The punctuation is surface; the whole clue is wordplay, defined only by the asterisk.
explanation.definitionFit: The asterisk marks a character in the preamble's opera: the Sergeant of Police leads the constables in The Pirates of Penzance.

clue.text: *Concise eponym of the last to incur spiritual punishment — one to boast about

indicators.note: to incur something is to take it on, so the punishment takes the letter into itself

parts.note: penance is the punishment imposed for sin
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: about means the boasting word goes round the numeral on either side

parts.note: to prate is to talk boastfully and at length
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A tangled description of a sinner who deserves his spiritual penalty and a braggart to boast of.
explanation.walkthrough: PEN(Z)ANCE then P(I)RATE. The opera is The Pirates of Penzance, so a single Penzance pirate is the title cut down to one person.
explanation.definitionFit: The opera takes its title from these characters, so one of them is a shortened version of the name it is called by.

clue.text: Page American comrade of vernal appearance

parts.note: a leaf is a page of a book
bud is American slang for a pal

explanation.surface: A young page from the United States and his spring-like friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf bud is the swelling on a twig that opens into a leaf, one of the first signs of spring.

clue.text: Tea with fruit, in which is the end of the colour changer

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: in which is says the fruit holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a melon is a fruit

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the word itself supplies its last letter

explanation.surface: A tea party with fruit, at which something that changes colour turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA then MEL(E)ON. The second 'the' is both part of the surface and the word whose end is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: The lizard is famous for altering its skin colour to suit mood or surroundings.

clue.text: School subject, footwear, in which top of class

indicators.note: in which means the footwear holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: a sandal is an open shoe

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of class

explanation.surface: A list of things at school: a subject, shoes, and who came top of the class.
explanation.walkthrough: S(C)ANDAL. The definition is a joke: Sheridan's comedy is called The School for Scandal, so scandal is that school's subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan's play The School for Scandal names an imaginary school whose lesson is gossip and slander.

clue.text: Echo, only more so, under the bit

parts.note: re, the note in sol-fa, taken as a little bit of a tune
in this down entry the noise word sits under the note

explanation.surface: A horsey description of an animal answering the bit even more readily than before.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose Araucaria clue: in a down light 'under' puts one piece below the other, and 'the bit' is a scrap of music. To resound is to echo loudly and at length.
explanation.definitionFit: Resounding means ringing with repeated noise, a fuller, louder form of what an echo does.

clue.text: I didn't catch what you said about painting the planet

indicators.note: about means the exclamation goes round the other word on both sides

parts.words: I didn't catch what you said
parts.note: eh is what you say when you missed something
painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: Someone mishears a remark about a picture of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: E(ART)H.
explanation.definitionFit: Our own world is the third planet from the Sun, the one people live on.

clue.text: Accidental exposure of card demands response from FDR

definitions.meaning: first meaning: at the card table, a card shown by mistake means the hands must be dealt again
second meaning: Roosevelt's programme answering the Great Depression

explanation.surface: A president caught flashing a card at the table must answer for it.
explanation.walkthrough: If a card is exposed during the deal, the rules call for the cards to be dealt afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Franklin Roosevelt's 1930s reform programme, his answer to economic collapse, was named the New Deal.

clue.text: *Subtitle for faulty votes he'd exposed

indicators.note: the letters are laid open and set out afresh, exposed in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, all fourteen letters

explanation.surface: A politician's dodgy votes are found out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' looks like the anagram signal but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The opera's full title is The Pirates of Penzance, or The Slave of Duty, so this phrase is its second, alternative title.

clue.text: Falls back once more upon the Sun

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for once more from right to left

parts.note: again means once more
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles over again in the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' looks like a verb but is the noun, the waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara Falls is the great waterfall on the border between Canada and the United States.

clue.text: Exclamation canonising *the maid of all work, say

parts.note: canonising makes someone a saint, ST

indicators.note: say tells us to go by the name as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: Ruth is the pirates' maid of all work in the opera

explanation.surface: A cry of surprise at a humble servant being made a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: ST plus REWTH, said like Ruth. The asterisk marks Ruth as a character in the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewth is an old oath of surprise, a contraction of God's truth, still common in Australia.

clue.text: Walk *the first of 25's 12 out

indicators.note: out suggests the name is knocked out of its usual shape and reset

parts.note: Major-General Stanley's eldest daughter in the opera

explanation.surface: The general's eldest daughter goes out for a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is GENERAL STANLEY and 12 is DAUGHTERS; his first daughter is Mabel, the heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk slowly and in a relaxed way, a leisurely stroll.

clue.text: Disgusting expression among those arranging to meet *25's

indicators.note: among means the exclamation sits in the middle of the people

parts.note: people making dates
ugh is the noise of disgust

explanation.surface: A grimace of distaste among the people fixing up dates with the general's girls.
explanation.walkthrough: D(UGH)ATERS. 25 is General Stanley, whose many daughters the pirates hope to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Major-General Stanley's wards in the opera are his daughters, a chorus of girls led by Mabel.

clue.text: What is chewed, set and beaten

parts.note: cud is what cattle chew
gelled means set like a jelly

explanation.surface: A recipe of sorts: something chewed, left to firm up, then whisked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' sounds like kitchen whisking; it means struck with a club.
explanation.definitionFit: To cudgel someone is to hit them repeatedly with a short thick stick.

clue.text: Dame that took the first of 25's 12?

indicators.note: the name was taken over and remade, as a performer takes a stage name

parts.note: the general's eldest daughter

explanation.surface: A great lady singer who took on the role of the general's eldest daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the fancy: a soprano might sing Mabel, and her own name is that name rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Nellie Melba was the Australian soprano, made a Dame of the British Empire in 1918.

clue.text: Sensational affair for older characters among mothers

indicators.note: among means the jumbled letters go in the middle of the mothers

parts.note: two mothers, MA and MA

indicators.note: only the characters of the word are used, free to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A scandalous episode involving older people in a group of mothers.
explanation.walkthrough: The mixed letters go between the two mothers, after the first M rather than between MA and MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is an overwrought, exaggerated play or situation full of sensation.

clue.text: It's obvious what *the maid of all work proved to be

definitions.text: what *the maid of all work proved to be
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in the opera Frederic finds that Ruth is no beauty

explanation.walkthrough: Ruth told the young Frederic she was beautiful; once he sees other women he finds she is not good-looking at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both clear and evident, and homely or unattractive in looks.

clue.text: Characteristic of wandering mind and warming heart?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as in ... of mind, daydreaming
second meaning: the proverb says it makes the heart grow fonder

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'absence makes the heart grow fonder'; the question mark covers the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent-mindedness is a mind elsewhere, and being away from someone, by the saying, deepens affection.

clue.text: Old warrior has this tough old bird in hand

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the weapon an ancient fighter carries in his hand
second meaning: a fierce, domineering older woman

explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is British slang for a woman, not a fowl.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a broad-bladed war weapon and, figuratively, an aggressive, formidable older woman.

clue.text: Don't allow lawyers a girl

parts.note: to bar is to forbid
the Bar is the body of barristers
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction not to let the legal profession near a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbara is a common female first name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Solver's rights to states held by Greek god

parts.note: the solver is 'you', and thy is the old word for your
R for right, twice over
the United States

explanation.surface: A complaint that the reader's rights to various states are being held back by a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The thyrsus is the ivy-tipped staff carried by Dionysus, Greek god of wine, and his followers.

clue.text: Bill, Maud and pal, topped not tailed

indicators.note: topped means the head is cut off, as when topping and tailing beans

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Three friends going through vegetables: the ends topped but not the tails.
explanation.walkthrough: Only Maud and pal lose their first letters; Bill is replaced by its abbreviation. The phrase echoes 'topped and tailed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acaudal is the zoological term for having no tail, from Latin cauda, tail.

clue.text: Blown fruit

parts.note: surface reading: fruit that is overripe or puffed up
setter's reading: the rude noise made by blowing through pursed lips is named after a berry

explanation.walkthrough: Blowing a raspberry is the rude tongue noise, from rhyming slang raspberry tart.
explanation.definitionFit: The berry gives its name to the derisive spluttering noise, which is always described as blown.

clue.text: *The first of 25's 12 may take the rap

indicators.note: the name is taken and reworked into a different order

parts.note: the general's eldest daughter

explanation.surface: The general's eldest daughter may end up punished for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take the rap' looks like the definition; the definition is just 'the rap'.
explanation.definitionFit: To take the rap is to accept the blame, so the rap is responsibility for a fault.

clue.text: There's little character in old warfare

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Ancient battles had no room for personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little character' reads as a lack of personality; it is a small person in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwarf is a very short figure in fairy tales, a small person in a story.

clue.text: Beat Jack with a flourish (*1 across's men put in the big guns)

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
jack and tar are both words for a sailor
taken as written

explanation.surface: Thrash a sailor with a fanfare, while the policemen are sent in to man the cannon.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket points to the opera: the Sergeant's policemen march off singing 'Tarantara', a trumpet call, to face the pirates.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantara is a blare of trumpets or horns, a fanfare announcing someone.

clue.text: Extend across the opening of 12 in Berlin

indicators.note: only the opening is kept; the rest of the word is dropped

parts.note: to span is to stretch across
the answer at 12 across

explanation.surface: Stretch across the start of the daughters' row in the German capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first three letters of the 12 answer are kept, a loose 'opening'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spandau is a western borough of Berlin, known for its prison that held Nazi war criminals.

clue.text: *Major public port that's capital

parts.note: general means common to everyone, public
Stanley, the harbour capital of the Falkland Islands

explanation.surface: A large public harbour that also serves as a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' looks like an adjective, important; in the opera he is the Major-General, so 'Major' is his rank's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Major-General Stanley is the opera's 'very model of a modern Major-General', so the rank's first word points to him.
